problem.text: Conlon and Lee's question whether every weakly norming graph is edge-transitive.

claims.text: Theorem 1: every weakly norming graph is edge-transitive.

assumptions.text: Hatami's biregularity theorem, Lovasz's Holder characterization, and the fact that homomorphism densities determine a graph up to isomorphism.

methods.text: A first-order perturbation argument shows that all edge-deleted subgraphs have equal densities and are therefore isomorphic; the isomorphisms are upgraded to automorphisms.

limitations.text: Edge-transitivity is necessary, not sufficient; the Sidorenko property of edge-transitive non-norming graphs is not addressed.

relevance.text: Fixes the hierarchy weakly norming implies edge-transitive implies biregular, which the symmetric candidates of this exploration (edge-transitive or biregular graphs) sit on.
